claims.text: Non-equiatomic high-entropy alloys possess inherent chemical disorder that affects their baseline magnetic and magnetocaloric behavior.
Selective replacement of magnetic elements with non-magnetic elements can tune chemical disorder in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Controlled thermal processing can tune chemical disorder in non-equiatomic HEAs.
Elemental substitution and tailored annealing can modify short-range magnetic correlations.
Changing chemical disorder adjusts magnetic exchange interactions.
Replacing magnetic elements with non-magnetic elements modifies the density of magnetic exchange sites.
Replacing magnetic elements with non-magnetic elements modifies the spatial distribution of magnetic exchange sites.
Modification of magnetic exchange sites alters the ferromagnetic-to-paramagnetic transition temperature.
The combined changes induced by substitution and annealing influence the magnetocaloric response.
The proposed compositional and thermal interventions will cause a measurable shift in magnetic transition temperature.
The proposed interventions will enhance the magnetocaloric effect relative to the initial alloy state.
The tuning effect occurs only within a restricted compositional-substitution window.
The tuning effect occurs only within a controlled thermal-processing regime.
Extreme elemental substitution may cause phase separation.
Extreme substitution or annealing conditions may degrade magnetic properties.
Existing evidence supports the proposition that compositional tuning and annealing affect magnetocaloric behavior.
